text:
Ben: Heads up — a partner asked why their Dedicated "burst" credits dropped even though traffic was mostly to a pinned model. They see throttles on some API keys in the same org. Can we clarify how credits flow across tenant/project boundaries?

Dima: Are they using multiple API keys under one org? Current model: reserved_throughput applies at org level, burst credits are pooled per-reservation. Keys inherit allowance but we do per-key inflight counters for fairness.

Eva: Customer complaint is UI/visibility more than policy. They want to see which key consumed credits. Can we add per-key breakdown in Console and /metrics?

Ben: Exactly. Right now billing shows org-level consumption which confuses them. Need both telemetry (internal) and UI (customer-facing).

Alicia: Policy question: do we want to keep burst as a pooled org-level bank or a per-key bucket with overdraft fallback? Pooled is simpler for soft fairness but hard for tenants that expect isolation.

Frank: From accounting side, pooled org-bank is fine but we must mark consumption with "origin_key" tag for invoicing/export. Also need a coarse-grained chargeback export for customers running multi-tenant workloads.

Dima: Technical concern: tagging every token emission with origin_key increases metrics cardinality. Suggest: tag for sampling and aggregate by 1m windows. Also add a lightweight counter that increments per-request: 
```
rate_limit.update({"org_id": org, "api_key": key_id, "model": model_name}, tokens)
```
we can emit sampled histograms to avoid high cardinality.

Eva: For Console UX: show "Burst bank" with a small per-key flyout that indicates recent top consumers (last 24h top 5 keys) and a link to raw logs. That should reduce support tickets.

Alicia: Rollout plan? We need design + infra + API changes. Proposal: Phase 1 — internal-only telemetry + sampling (no customer UI). Phase 2 — console visibility and opt-in per-key buckets. Phase 3 — policy toggle (org-pool vs per-key) for beta customers.

Ben: Sounds reasonable. Dima, what modules touch the rate limiter? I can open a PR but need pointers.

Dima: rate-limiter lives in inference-gateway (go) and quota-service (python). Quota-service has account-level bank logic. Gateway enforces inflight and per-key limits. You'd need changes in both: emit tags in quota-service, add sampled metrics in gateway.

Ben: Quick prototype snippet to emit a sampled metric from gateway (Go):
```go
if rand.Float64() < 0.01 {
  metrics.Emit("burst.consume", float64(tokens), map[string]string{"org": orgID, "key": keyID})
}
```
This keeps cardinality low.

Dima: +1 for sampling. Also add a deterministic sampler for high-volume keys so we always capture top consumers.

Frank: For export, add a CSV export endpoint in billing that sums sampled counts and estimates total using sampling rate. We can label exports "estimated" vs "exact".

Eva: UX note: indicate sampling/estimate in console so customers don't mistake numbers for exact billing. Maybe a tooltip: "Values are sampled for performance; contact support for exact logs."

infra-bot: deploy-gateway/2026-03-18T09:12:08Z started (sha: ab12cd). CI: all green.

Alicia: Owners? Ben = product/coord, Dima = infra lead, Eva = UX, Frank = billing. Can we get rough ETA?

Ben: I'll draft a short RFC today and link to this thread. Target: phase1 in 3 weeks, phase2 in 8 weeks if no blockers.

Dima: I'll audit hotspots for tagging overhead and file a perf checklist.

Frank: I'll draft export columns and sample-adjustment formula.

Eva: I'll do mockups for the flyout and sampling disclosure.

Ben: Great — thanks everyone. I'll ping @Alicia for prioritization in roadmap sync. :thumbsup:
